title: Integrate cross-language SDK publishing pipeline with provenance/signing, streaming ergonomics, and retry examples
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
We need a single, auditable CI/publishing pipeline that builds and publishes Redwood SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Go with reproducible provenance metadata and artifact signing. This ticket covers: (a) publishing flows to PyPI/npm/Go modules, (b) in-repo examples that demonstrate streaming ergonomics and recommended retry policies, (c) embedding SBOM/provenance and signing artifacts, and (d) CI gating for releases and automated smoke tests.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals: Consistent versioning strategy (semver), deterministic build artifacts + provenance (in-toto/Provenance attestation), automated signing (cosign or GPG), publishing automation, and SDK examples that show streaming + retry best-practices across all three languages.
- Non-goals: Changing public API shape for existing customers (we will keep compatibility and provide adapters), full enterprise-only private registry automation (follow-up ticket).

Key decisions / trade-offs discussed:
- Use semver for SDKs and tag release branches with pattern "sdk/v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}". Rationale: aligns with developer expectations and makes rollbacks trivial.
- Use GitHub Actions as central CI since artifacts and PATs are already stored there; use self-hosted runners for language-specific native builds where needed (Go module proxy tests, Python wheels on manylinux).
- Use cosign for artifact signing and in-toto provenance attestations for each packaged artifact. Alternative (sigstore GPG-only) considered but cosign + in-toto provides better CI integration and registries support for npm/PyPI.
- Publish npm packages with 2FA-enabled account; PyPI publishing uses API token scoped to project; Go modules use authenticated tags and GOPROXY validation.

Work plan / checklist (high level):
- [x] Draft versioning and release tag convention (this PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/compare/release-conventions)
- [x] Create baseline CI workflow to build wheels, tarballs, npm packages, and go mod checks (GH Actions: .github/workflows/ci-sdk-build.yml)
- [ ] Implement cosign signing step and upload provenance attestations to GCS (or S3) with retention policy
- [ ] Add canonical SBOM generation (Syft) and attach to release artifacts
- [ ] Add language-specific smoke tests for published packages (pip install from test index, npm install from npm test registry, go get with GOPRIVATE overrides)
- [ ] Add streaming ergonomics examples to examples/streaming/{python,ts,go} demonstrating client-side fragment assembly, backpressure, and reconnect semantics
- [ ] Add documented retry policy examples and SDK helpers: exponential backoff + jitter, idempotency key guidance for replays, and streaming resume tokens
- [ ] Update SDK README and release instructions, plus a Confluence doc for security review

Implementation notes and TODOs by area:
- CI / Build:
  - Build matrix for Python: CPython 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 using manylinux wheels. Create wheel and sdist.
  - TS: build tarball, test transpiled bundle for both ESM/CJS consumers.
  - Go: run `go test ./...` and `goreleaser` for module packaging; validate go.sum reproducibility.
  - Make ephemeral test PyPI/npm registries available for CI smoke tests (use TestPyPI and npm install --registry).
  - Keep artifact metadata flat JSON (name, version, sha256, cosign signature URL, sbom URL, provenance URL) and attach to GH Release.

- Signing/Provenance:
  - Use sigstore/cosign in GitHub Actions with OIDC to avoid long-lived secrets where possible. For local/enterprise private flows, fallback to HSM/KMS-based signing and record KMS key IDs.
  - Generate in-toto link metadata for each build step; store build recipe and builder identity.
  - Store provenance metadata in an S3/GCS bucket prefixed by release tag. Add lifecycle policy (90 days hot, then cold).

- Streaming ergonomics + retries (SDK changes):
  - Python: add StreamingClient context manager that yields an async generator with built-in reconnect and resume token handling. Expose `retry_config` param and helper `RetryPolicy` with standard jitter/backoff.
  - TypeScript: provide both callback and async-iterator idioms; implement `streamingClient.stream()` that returns an AsyncIterable with `cancel()` & `resume(token)` helpers.
  - Go: expose a channel-based API with context-aware cancellation; streaming client returns a struct with `Recv()` and `Resume(token)` and built-in reconnect/backoff.
  - Provide example prompt sets showing how to resume after partial responses and how to deduplicate tokens on retry.

- Examples and docs:
  - Add three canonical examples under examples/streaming demonstrating canonical patterns for handling partial texts, function/tool calling in streaming, and integrating local caches for prefix reuse.
  - Create a snippet repo for quickstarts: `redwood-inference/sdk-examples` and link from SDK README.

Acceptance criteria / Definition of Done:
- CI pipeline builds artifacts for Python/TS/Go reproducibly and emits an artifacts.json with SHA256 checksums and provenance links.
- Artifacts are signed with cosign and signatures are verifiable via demo steps in README.
- PyPI/npm/Go publish steps execute in a dry-run to test staging registries, and smoke test installs pass within CI.
- Streaming examples present in repo with language parity and documented retry primitives.
- Security review sign-off recorded in Confluence and security checklist attached to release.

Progress updates / recent activity:
- 2025-02-20: Spike completed to validate cosign + in-toto in GH Actions (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/198).
- 2025-02-25: Prototype streaming helper added for Python, awaiting API review from SDKs team (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/205).
- 2025-03-03: TS streaming API shape proposal discussed in sync; agreed on AsyncIterator + cancel semantics. Action: update TS README examples.
- 2025-03-04: Began implementing SBOM generation step; syft integration branch created (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/220).

Open questions / risks:
- Private deployment signing: customers using on-prem may require local signing keys (HSM). Need to document offline signing integration and support matrix.
- PyPI 2FA requirements: ensure service account and automation are compliant; we may need an org-level maintainer flow.
- Backward compatibility: streaming API changes must provide adapters for v1 users; add migration guide.

Next immediate steps (this week):
- Implement cosign OIDC step in ci-sdk-build.yml and test on a draft tag (owner: Liam Chen).
- Finish Python streaming PR feedback and merge example into examples/streaming/python (owner: Priya Nair).
- Add smoke test job to publish to TestPyPI and install in a fresh virtualenv (owner: QA Team).

Notes for reviewer:
- Please prioritize security reviewers for the cosign configuration and the bucket ACLs for provenance artifacts.
- Validate that the streaming helper API meets client ergonomics expectations: we prefer minimal ceremony for common cases (simple for-loop consumption), while exposing hooks for advanced resume/backpressure management.

Follow-ups / future improvements:
- Automate cross-repo release notes generation and change logs by parsing PR labels and linking to artifacts.json.
- Add a developer CLI to locally produce signed artifacts for release candidates.
